clue.text: Stratagem and skill shown by diplomat in charge

parts.note: tact is the delicate handling of people that a diplomat needs

explanation.surface: A clever ploy, combining guile with the finesse of the diplomat running the negotiations.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactic is a planned manoeuvre to gain an advantage, which is what a stratagem is.

clue.text: Creature displaying power in landscape

indicators.note: the letter for power is placed inside the word for landscape

parts.note: terrain is a stretch of land considered for its physical features
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: An animal is shown off against a scenic backdrop.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrapin is a small freshwater turtle, an animal of the reptile kind.

clue.text: Offence unsettling the heart of America?

indicators.note: something unsettled is disturbed, so the letters picked out are thrown into a new order
the heart of a word is everything except its first and last letters, here taken from America

explanation.surface: A provocative act shakes the American heartland, ending in a question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the heart of' gives MERIC, the middle of AMERICA, and 'unsettling' rearranges those five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A crime is an unlawful act, a breach of the law, so an offence.

clue.text: Vain eccentric standing on promontory in novel

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece standing on another sits above it
eccentric means odd or irregular, so the letters of vain are put in an odd order

parts.note: a hoe is a projecting point of land, found in place names like Plymouth Hoe

explanation.surface: A conceited oddball stands atop a headland in a work of fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing on' works only in a down entry, where the first piece sits on top of the second; 'eccentric' rearranges the word vain, and 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivanhoe is the historical novel by Sir Walter Scott, an example of the form.

clue.text: Retired toff, important historian

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: a toff is a posh person, also called a nob
big can mean important, as in a big name

explanation.surface: A grand gentleman who has retired, a figure of note, is listed as a chronicler of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' turns NOB plus BIG, NOBBIG, end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Gibbon wrote The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire, so he is a famous example of a chronicler.

clue.text: Coaxed at home French aristocrat with journalist

parts.note: someone who is in is at home
duc is the French word for a duke
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A French nobleman was talked into something at his house by a reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: To induce someone is to persuade or prevail upon them, which is what coaxing does.

clue.text: One in charge of local trade?

definitions.text: One in charge of local trade?

parts.words: One in charge of local trade?
parts.note: read local as a pub, as in British slang, and the person in charge of trade there is one who looks after the counter where drinks are served

explanation.surface: Someone who runs commerce in the neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' is British slang for one's nearby pub, not the adjective it seems to be.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who tends the counter in a pub serves the drinks, the main trade done there.

clue.text: Principle that is barely followed?

parts.note: barely suggests hardly at all, but read literally it means in the bare, naked: a belief practised without clothes

explanation.surface: A rule hardly anybody keeps to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barely' seems to mean scarcely, but it is to be read as unclothed.
explanation.definitionFit: Nudism is the practice or creed of going without clothes, a way of life its followers adopt in the bare.

clue.text: Closely connected room east of renovated marina

indicators.note: in an across answer, east of means to the right of, so the room abbreviation comes after
renovated means done up and rebuilt, so the letters of marina are rearranged

explanation.surface: A property listing: a room overlooking a smartened-up harbour, tightly linked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'east of' is a map direction: in an across entry it means placed to the right; 'renovated' signals the rearrangement of marina.
explanation.definitionFit: People walking with linked limbs are physically joined, so the phrase means intimately associated.

clue.text: Lid put on old-fashioned college resident?

definitions.text: Lid put on old-fashioned college resident?

parts.words: Lid put on old-fashioned college resident?
parts.note: lid is slang for a hat, and this one is the square academic cap traditionally worn by those living in a college

explanation.surface: A cover is placed on a quaint student boarder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lid' is slang for a hat, and 'put on' means worn, not placed on top of.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortarboard is a flat square academic cap with a tassel, worn traditionally by university students and staff.

clue.text: Ridicule a good deal of wilder ideas

indicators.note: a good deal of says most but not all of the letters of the phrase wilder ideas are taken

explanation.surface: Mock a large share of some rather crazy notions.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the word break: wilDER IDEas.
explanation.definitionFit: To deride is to mock with contempt, a synonym of ridicule used as a verb.

clue.text: Punish students in passage

definitions.meaning: at Oxford and Cambridge, to confine undergraduates to college as a penalty
an opening in a wall or fence through which one passes

explanation.surface: Discipline pupils in the corridor.
explanation.definitionFit: Gating was the traditional university penalty of confining students, and a gate is an entrance way through a barrier.

clue.text: Edam? Bad luck!

definitions.meaning: Edam is a firm Dutch variety, an example of the type
an unsympathetic British exclamation meaning tough luck

explanation.surface: A cheese, and a commiseration for someone who wanted something else.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is British slang, often said with little sympathy.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a firm cheese, and the phrase is also a British expression of mock commiseration.

clue.text: Without help, design handle with difficulty

indicators.note: something done with difficulty is wrestled into shape, so the letters of design and handle are rearranged

explanation.surface: Unaided, someone struggles to plan a grip for a door.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something single-handed means doing it alone, without any assistance.

clue.text: Ancient outbreak of tragic ire

indicators.note: an outbreak is a sudden eruption, so the letters of tragic and ire burst into a new order

explanation.surface: Long ago there was an eruption of awful rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Geriatric is used informally to mean very old, relating to old age.

clue.text: Useless quality in fellow heading water company?

indicators.note: heading means leading or going first, so the abbreviation for fellow comes before the rest

parts.note: a utility is a company providing a public service such as water

explanation.surface: Something pointless about a man who runs a water board.
explanation.definitionFit: Futility is the state of being pointless or ineffective, the condition of having no use.

clue.text: Artist in London area touching old woman? I'm tickled!

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist
Bow is a district in East London
old trout is a disparaging British term for an old woman

explanation.surface: A painter in East London is close to an elderly lady, who is delighted.
explanation.walkthrough: Tickling is a method of catching trout by hand, so the definition is the fish speaking. TROUT is from 'old trout', British slang for a cantankerous old woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglers catch this fish by tickling, stroking its belly by hand until it can be scooped out.

clue.text: Artist brought to second entrance

parts.note: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was a French painter

explanation.surface: A painter is taken to the side door.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingress is the act or means of going in, a formal word for a way in.

clue.text: Jam makers live north of church in market town

indicators.note: in a down answer, north of means above, so the verb comes before the church abbreviation

parts.note: the WI, or Women's Institute, is a British women's organisation famous for making jam, here in the plural
to be is to exist, to live

explanation.surface: Women who make preserves live above a church in a provincial town.
explanation.walkthrough: The WI is the Women's Institute, a British society known for jam; WISBECH is a market town in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisbech is a Fenland town in Cambridgeshire with a long-standing market.

clue.text: Test I have for a reason

parts.note: the MOT is the annual roadworthiness check on British cars
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: An exam that I have sat for a good cause.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is Britain's annual safety test for vehicles over three years old.
explanation.definitionFit: A motive is what prompts someone to act, the reason behind it.

clue.text: Sing a carol wrongly? Find source of notes

indicators.note: singing wrongly means getting it out of order, so the letters of sing a carol are jumbled

explanation.surface: A singer's festive song goes off-key, so look for where the tune comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: The cor anglais is a woodwind instrument of the oboe family, which produces musical sounds.

clue.text: One with inclination to drop a bird

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: to drop means to let go, so the letter named is taken out

parts.note: a bias is a leaning or tendency

explanation.surface: Someone tending to let a bird fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to drop' removes the A from BIAS, leaving BIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-legged wading bird with a downcurved bill.

clue.text: I roundly criticise religion

parts.note: to slam is to criticise severely, roundly meaning thoroughly

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a faith in no uncertain terms.
explanation.definitionFit: Islam is the monotheistic faith founded on the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad.

clue.text: Intense fool abandoning cooked fricassee

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or falsified, so the remaining letters are rearranged
abandoning means leaving behind, so the letters for fool are removed from the dish

parts.note: an ass is a foolish person

explanation.surface: A clumsy cook passionately gives up on preparing a stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' removes ASS from FRICASSEE to leave FRICEE, which 'cooked' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Fierce can mean extreme or very strong, as in fierce heat, so it matches intense.

clue.text: Secretly devised material at end of letter

indicators.note: one piece at the end of another comes after it

parts.note: dee is the spelt-out name of the letter D
plaid is a tartan cloth

explanation.surface: Cloth added at the bottom of a piece of correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep-laid plan is one worked out carefully in secret, a scheme laid well in advance.

clue.text: Overlook old partner, rod, holding spades

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or lover

indicators.note: holding means containing, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a cue is the rod used in snooker or billiards
S is the card-game abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: A former lover, carrying a stick with a digging tool, gets let off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' signals the container: the snooker rod wraps round the spades abbreviation, and the former partner leads.
explanation.definitionFit: To excuse a fault is to forgive it or let it pass, a synonym for overlooking it.

clue.text: Odd greeting by feminist in Wyoming

indicators.note: the greeting and the feminist are placed inside the abbreviation for the state

parts.note: WY is the postal abbreviation for Wyoming
hi is a casual greeting
Ms is the title favoured by many feminists

explanation.surface: A strange hello from a women's rights campaigner out in the American West.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an adjective: whimsy is listed in Chambers as an adjective meaning whimsical.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, the word means fanciful or quaint, so peculiar.
